caption:
Leonardo AI gives free users 150 tokens a day for AI images, and they reset every 24 hours.
Type a prompt, start in Fast mode, and save Ultra for the image you actually want.

site_article.headline: How to use Leonardo AI for free: prompts, Fast vs Ultra and the 150 daily tokens
site_article.dek: Leonardo AI makes images from text in your browser. Here is how to get a good result on the free plan without burning your daily tokens.
site_article.summary: Leonardo AI is an image and video generator that gives free users 150 tokens a day, reset every 24 hours. Type a prompt on the home page, try ideas in Fast mode, and upscale the one you like.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Leonardo AI for free: a step by step guide

paragraphs.text: How to use Leonardo AI, in short: type what you want to see into the prompt box on the home page and click Generate. Leonardo picks a model for you and makes the image. Free accounts get 150 tokens a day, which reset every 24 hours, and every image costs some of them.

Leonardo.Ai is an image and video generator that started in Sydney in 2022. Canva bought it in July 2024, but it still runs as a separate product with its own plans, and its models also power parts of Canva's Magic Studio, according to Krea's review of the service.

The free plan is good enough to learn the tool and make social posts or mood boards. It is not private, and the daily cap means you have to plan a little. The steps below are about getting more good images out of the same 150 tokens.
How to make your first image in Leonardo AI

paragraphs.title: 1. Sign up and type a prompt
paragraphs.text: Create an account at leonardo.ai. On the home page, click the prompt box, describe the image, and click Generate. This quick mode chooses a model it thinks fits your prompt, so you do not have to pick anything yet.

paragraphs.title: 2. Open the AI Image Creation tool for more control
paragraphs.text: Click the image option under the prompt bar, or choose it from the left sidebar. The sidebar there holds the real settings: the model, the generation mode, image dimensions, the number of images and a Collection to save them in. Which options you see depends on the model. On the free plan, the help center says the Models menu offers Auto Image or Auto Video.

paragraphs.title: 3. Pick Fast or Ultra
paragraphs.text: Fast is the cheaper mode for quick ideas. Ultra makes higher fidelity images and costs more tokens. Leonardo's own advice is to explore in Fast, then run your favorite through the Universal Upscaler instead of generating everything in Ultra.

paragraphs.title: 4. Check the cost before you click
paragraphs.text: The Generate button shows how many tokens the current settings will use. Fewer images per batch and smaller dimensions cost less. If a setting doubles the number, keep it for images that need it.

paragraphs.title: 5. Find, edit and download your images
paragraphs.text: Finished images land in the AI Creation feed and in your Library. Hover over one to upscale it, share it, download it, edit it, or turn it into a video.
How to write a Leonardo AI prompt that works

Leonardo's help center breaks a good prompt into five parts: the subject, the medium (for example an oil painting), the style (for example realism), the composition (pose, framing and focus) and the color and lighting. Most strong prompts include most of these.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: Leonardo's own five-part example
paragraphs.text: Realistic oil painting of a grumpy man in a seated pose, slightly off-center, focusing on facial expressions, with natural, muted colors and soft ambient lighting

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: The same pattern for a product photo
paragraphs.text: Photograph of [your product] on a [surface], centered, shot from slightly above, clean minimal style, with soft daylight from the left and a pale [color] background

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: The same pattern for a social post
paragraphs.text: Flat digital illustration of [subject] doing [action], bold graphic style, subject on the left third with empty space on the right for text, bright [color] and [color] palette with even lighting

For ideas, leave the prompt bar empty, click the dice icon and choose New Random Prompt. Or type a short idea like an orange cat and use Improve Prompt, then look at which details it added. Both are free ways to learn what the models respond to.
Open images in the Community Feed and click them to see the prompts behind them. It is the fastest way to find a style you like and copy its structure, not its exact words.

Leonardo also says that even a strong prompt often gets an image about 95% right. Fix the rest with the Canvas editor instead of spending more tokens on new attempts. Canvas supports inpainting, which regenerates only a selected area, and outpainting, which extends the borders.
What the free plan gets you, and what it does not

The free plan gives 150 tokens a day. They reset every 24 hours and, according to Krea's review, do not roll over, so unused tokens are lost at the reset. Paid plans get a monthly allowance instead, and paid users can buy top-up packs that never expire while the subscription is active.

Free images are public. Private mode, which hides your generations from the public feed, is listed in the help center as a paid feature. Ownership also depends on the plan: Krea's review of the terms says paid users own their outputs, while on the free plan ownership stays with Leonardo and free users get a commercial license to their images. Read the current terms before you use a free image for a client.

Where Leonardo falls short: video and third party models eat tokens fast, so 150 a day does not go far there. Reviewers also find that Midjourney gets a strong look with less effort, while Leonardo rewards people who are willing to tweak settings and prompts. If you want quick, pretty images and do not care about privacy, the free plan is fine. If your images are for work, the public feed alone is a reason to pay or pick another tool.

A simple daily routine for the free plan: try four or five ideas in Fast mode, pick one, fix small problems in Canvas, and only then upscale it. That keeps most of your tokens for the image you actually use.
